para.emphasis: Antimicrobial activity of YZ462 in cellular models

chapter.para: RAW264.7 cell was culture in 12-well plate (1×106/well) for 24h. Exponentially growing S. aureus MRS153 was harvested and washed three times with DMEM medium. Resuspended S. aureus MRS153 was used for infecting RAW264.7 cell for 3 h. Then the cells were washed three times with DMEM medium. Cells were incubated in 37℃with 5% CO2, YZ462 (8×MIC) was added as the experiment groups, isometric DMSO was added as the control groups. RAW264.7 cells were lysed with RIPA buffer every 30 min used for CFU determined.

para.emphasis: PI Staining Analysis in Eukaryotic cell line

chapter.para: HEK293T and Hela cells were treated with YZ462 and DMSO for 24 h at 37 °C and 5% CO2. PI (5 μg/mL) were added incubated at dark for 20 min, the cells were washed three times with DMEM medium before flow cytometry.

To test the interaction between PE or CL and compound YZ462, a calorimetric assay was performed by PEAQ-ITC at 25℃. PE was dissolved in 10% DMSO (2.0 mM) or CL was dissolved in EtOH (2.0 mM), which was sequentially injected into the calorimetric cells filled with compound YZ462 (0.2 mM), which was dissolved in the same buffer, and the injection was repeated 19 times with an equilibrium interval of 200 s. The equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) were obtained employing the relative software with the instrument.
[pic]

αReagents and conditions: (a) K2CO3, DMF, 60 ℃; (b) 3-thiopheneboronic acid, Pd(PPh3)4, Na2CO3, EtOH/H2O, DME, 95 ℃; (c) Fe, NH4Cl, MeOH/H2O, 80 ℃; (d) 2-(bromomethyl)benzo[b]thiophene, K2CO3, DMF, 0 ℃; (e) 4,4,4-trifluoro-butanoyl chloride, 1,4-dioxane, 105 ℃; (f) BCl3, DCM, 0 ℃~r.t.

1-(benzyloxy)-4-bromo-2-nitrobenzene (3). A mixture compounds 4-bromo-2-nitrophenol (327.0 mg, 1.5 mmol) and K2CO3 (618.0 mg, 4.5 mmol) were dissolved in 2 mL of anhydrous DMF, then (bromomethyl)benzene (0.53 mL, 4.5 mmol) was dropwise, the mixture was stirred at 60 ℃ for 1 h. After the reaction was complete detected by TLC, the mixture was extracted with EA and H2O, and the separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried over Na2SO4, concentrated, and then was purified by column chromatography to give compound 3 (427.8 mg, 92.6% yield).

3-(4-(benzyloxy)-3-nitrophenyl)thiophene (4). A mixture of compound 3 (427.8 mg, 1.39 mmol) in 1,2-dimethoxyethane (5.0 mL) and anhydrous ethanol (8.0 mL), catalytic Pd(PPh3)4 was added at r.t., and then the vial was purged with Ar and stirred for 5 min. Subsequently, the 3-thiopheneboronic acid (355.6 mg, 2.78 mmol) and aqueous solution of Na2CO3 (2.0 mol/L, 10 mL) were then added to the mixture, and the vial was purged with Ar again, and the resulting mixture was heated to 95 °C for overnight. The residue was concentrated and the extracted with CH2Cl2 and H2O, and the separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried over Na2SO4, and was purified by column chromatography to give compound 4 (399.3 mg, 88.5% yield).

2-(benzyloxy)-5-(thiophen-3-yl)aniline (5). A mixture of compound 4 (399.3 mg, 1.28 mmol) in EtOH/H2O= 4:1 (10 mL) was added Fe (645.1 mg, 11.52 mmol) and NH4Cl (890.2 mg, 16.64 mmol), the reaction mixture was heated at 85 ℃ for 2 h, and then EtOH was evaporated under vacuum. The residue was extracted with ethyl acetate (EA) and H2O, and the separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried over Na2SO4, and evaporated to dryness to give crude compound 5 (296.4 mg, 82.3% yield).

N-(benzo[b]thiophen-2-ylmethyl)-2-(benzyloxy)-5-(thiophen-3-yl)aniline (6). To a solution of 1-benzothiophen-2-ylmethanol (456.45 mg, 3.0 mmol) in DCM (5.0 mL), PBr3 was then added at 0 ℃ for 10 min, and the reaction was quenched with water. The residue was extracted with CH2Cl2 and H2O, and the separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried over Na2SO4, and concentrated to obtain crud 2-(bromomethyl)benzo[b]thiophene (616.6 mg, yield 95.6%). Subsequently, a solution of compound 5 (296.4 mg, 1.05 mmol) and K2CO3 (291.18 mg, 2.1 mmol) in DMF (2 mL), and then 2-(bromomethyl)benzo[b]thiophene (238.47 mg, 1.05 mmol) was dropwise at 0 ℃, the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature for 5 h. After reaction was complete, the residue was extracted with CH2Cl2 and H2O, and the separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried over Na2SO4, concentrated, and then was purified by column chromatography to give compound 6 (330.9 mg, 73.2% yield).

N-(benzo[b]thiophen-2-ylmethyl)-N-(2-(benzyloxy)-5-(thiophen-3-yl)phenyl)-4,4,4-trifluorobutanamide (7). A solution of compound 6 (330.9 mg, 0.77 mmol) and 4,4,4-trifluorobutanoyl chloride (372.7 mg, 2.32 mmol) in 1,4-dioxane (10 mL). The mixture was stirred at 105 ℃ for 15 min. After reaction was complete, the 1,4-dioxane was evaporated under vacuum. The residue was extracted with CH2Cl2 and H2O, and the separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried over Na2SO4, concentrated, and then was purified by column chromatography to give compound 7 (378.5 mg, 89.1% yield).

N-(benzo[b]thiophen-2-ylmethyl)-4,4,4-trifluoro-N-(2-hydroxy-5-(thiophen-3-yl)phenyl)butanamide (YZ462). Compound 7 (378.5 mg, 0.69 mmol) in DCM (2.5 mL), then BCl3 was dropwise at 0 ℃. The mixture was stirred at room temperature until TLC indicated the reaction was complete, which then was quenched with water. The residue was extracted with CH2Cl2 and H2O, and the separated organic layer was washed with brine, dried over Na2SO4, concentrated, and then was purified by column chromatography to give YZ462 (251.6 mg, 79% yield). 1H NMR (300 MHz, CDCl3) δ 7.89 – 7.80 (m, 1H), 7.74 – 7.66 (m, 1H), 7.53 (dd, J = 8.5, 2.0 Hz, 1H), 7.36 (dd, J = 5.9, 3.1 Hz, 2H), 7.28 (d, J = 2.0 Hz, 1H), 7.26 – 7.23 (m, 1H), 7.16 – 7.02 (m, 4H), 5.41 (d, J = 14.9 Hz, 1H), 4.90 (d, J = 14.9 Hz, 1H), 2.60 – 2.43 (m, 4H). 13C NMR (75 MHz, DMSO-d6) δ 169.59 (s), 152.77 (s), 142.57 (s), 140.98 (s), 139.64 (s), 138.94 (s), 128.27 (s), 126.92 (s), 126.67 (s), 125.69 (s), 124.65 (s), 124.20 (d, J = 3.6 Hz), 123.60 (s), 123.32 (s), 122.56 (s), 122.35 (s), 117.37 (s), 46.99 (s), 28.37 (s), 25.83 (s). Fig. S1 Antimicrobial activity of YZ462 in cellular models. RAW264.7 cells were infected with exponentially growing S. aureus MRS153 and treated with YZ462 (8×MIC). CFU was checked every 30 min until 3 h.
[pic]
Fig. S2 YZ462 toxicity test in mice. Mice body weights were observed for 7 days after tail vein injection of 25 mg/kg or 50 mg/kg of YZ462.
[pic]
Fig. S3 Bacterial counting in the biofilm. The mature biofilms of S. aureus ATCC6538 (A) and MRS153 (B) were treated with YZ462 for 24 hours, followed by serial dilution and CFU counting.
[pic]

Fig. S4 Bactericidal activity of YZ462 is dependent on ROS production. DMSO counteracts compound YZ462-medicated lethality. Exponentially growing S. aureus ATCC6538 and MRS153 cells were treated with 5 μg/mL of compound YZ462 in the absence or presence of DMSO (5% or 7.5%).
[pic]

Fig. S5 Exponentially growing S. aureus ATCC6538 were preloaded with 5 μM H2DCFDA for 10 min. (A) S. aureus ATCC6538 was treated with DMSO (the volume is the same as that of YZ462), and sampled every 20 min for flow cytometry analysis after PBS washing. (B) The pretreated S. aureus ATCC 6538 was treated with YZ462 (5×MIC) and norfloxacin (5×MIC) for 60 min, followed by ROS level detection using flow cytometry.
[pic]

Fig. S6 Ciprofloxacin does not affect the cell membrane of S. aureus ATCC6538. (A) Cytometry detected of PI uptake by S. aureus ATCC6538 under the treatment with Ciprofloxacin or DMSO for 2 h (5 × MIC, 1.25 μg/mL).
[pic]
Fig. S7 YZ462 does not affect the cell membrane of eukaryotic cells. Cytometry detected of PI uptake by HEK293T and Hela cells under the treatment with YZ462 for 24 h (10 μg/mL).
[pic]
Fig. S8. YZ462 binding to CL and PE. Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) analysis of the interaction of CL (A) and PE (B) with compound YZ462.
